modern: How strangely men act! They will not praise those who are living at the same time and living with them; but to be praised themselves by posterity, by those whom they have never seen and never will see, this they set great value on. But this is very much the same as if you were to be upset because those who lived before you did not praise you.
original: How strangely men act! They will not praise those who are living at the same time and living with themselves; but to be themselves praised by posterity, by those whom they have never seen nor ever will see, this they set much value on. But this is very much the same as if thou shouldst be grieved because those who have lived before thee did not praise thee.

explained.summary: People are strange. They won’t praise the people living right alongside them, yet they badly want praise from future generations they’ll never meet. Marcus points out how absurd that is: it’s about as sensible as being upset that people who lived before you didn’t praise you.
explained.today: Think of people who chase a legacy or imagine how they’ll be remembered, while barely thanking the colleague at the next desk or the partner who cooks most nights. The appreciation that’s actually possible is the kind you give and get now.
